projects.title: Campus Café Checkout
projects.description: Turn a café order into an itemized invoice. Explore discounts, tax, and tips.
projects.focus: One change can affect several totals.
rules: Prices are stored in cents: 850 means $8.50. Quantities must be whole numbers from 0 to 99.
Student orders receive 10% off the subtotal. Other orders receive no discount.
Both 7% practice tax and the selected tip percentage use the discounted subtotal.
Round each percentage amount to the nearest cent, half up. Add the rounded tax and tip to the discounted subtotal.
projects.pseudocode:
READ customer
SET subtotal to 0
REPEAT for each of 3 menu items
    READ quantity
    ADD price × quantity to subtotal
READ student status and tip percentage
IF student, calculate discount
CALCULATE net, tax, tip, and total
PRINT the invoice

walk.title: Plan before coding
walk.explanation: Separate inputs (quantities and status), processing (multiply, discount, add), and output (the invoice). Manually predict one order before running it.
walk.snippet:
subtotal = 0
# Add the three item totals before applying a discount.

walk.title: Give values a job
walk.explanation: BURGER_PRICE is an integer number of cents. quantity is also an integer; multiplying them gives a line total. Uppercase names mark constants by convention, but Python still lets you change them.

walk.title: Make the receipt readable
walk.explanation: input() returns a string. strip() removes outer spaces; lower() lets YES and yes mean the same thing. An f-string inserts values. :.2f displays two digits after the decimal point.

walk.title: Choose a discount
walk.explanation: The condition selects one branch. With a $26.00 subtotal, yes gives a $2.60 discount; no gives $0.00. Changing the discount also changes the tax and tip bases.

walk.title: Repeat without losing the total
walk.explanation: range(1, 4) visits 1, 2, 3. subtotal is an accumulator and must start before the loop. The while loop in read_whole repeats until it receives a valid quantity.

walk.title: Reuse a calculation
walk.explanation: price and quantity are parameters in the definition. 850 and 2 are arguments in a call. return gives back 1700 cents. Printing a result and returning it are different actions.

# CAMPUS CAFE CHECKOUT | Introduction to Python | Professor Porras
# Classroom simulation: prices are cents; percentage rates are whole numbers.
# Input order: customer, burger qty, drink qty, dessert qty, student yes/no, tip %.
# Example input: Alex / 2 / 2 / 1 / yes / 15 (one value per line).

BURGER_PRICE = 850
DRINK_PRICE = 250
DESSERT_PRICE = 400
TAX_PERCENT = 7
STUDENT_DISCOUNT_PERCENT = 10

# MODULE 6: parameters receive arguments; return sends a result to the caller.
def money(cents):
    return f"${cents / 100:.2f}"

def percent_of(cents, percent):
    # Whole-cent, half-up rounding for nonnegative amounts: // is floor division.
    return (cents * percent + 50) // 100

def line_total(price, quantity):
    return price * quantity

def read_whole(label, minimum, maximum):
    # MODULES 3-5: clean text, make a decision, and repeat invalid input.
    while True:
        text = input().strip()
        if text.isascii() and text.isdigit():
            value = int(text)
            if minimum <= value <= maximum:
                return value
        print(f"Invalid {label}. Next input must be {minimum} to {maximum}.")

# MODULES 1-3: follow the algorithm, store values, and format strings.
customer = input().strip()
if customer == "":
    customer = "Guest"
subtotal = 0
receipt_lines = ""

# MODULE 5: range(1, 4) produces 1, 2, 3. Accumulate all three line totals.
for item in range(1, 4):
    # MODULE 4: choose exactly one name and price for this loop iteration.
    if item == 1:
        name = "Burger"
        price = BURGER_PRICE
    elif item == 2:
        name = "Drink"
        price = DRINK_PRICE
    else:
        name = "Dessert"
        price = DESSERT_PRICE
    quantity = read_whole(name + " quantity", 0, 99)
    amount = line_total(price, quantity)
    subtotal = subtotal + amount
    receipt_lines = receipt_lines + f"{name}: {quantity} x {money(price)} = {money(amount)}\n"

student = input().strip().lower()
while student != "yes" and student != "no":
    print("Student status: next input must be yes or no.")
    student = input().strip().lower()
tip_percent = read_whole("tip percent", 0, 100)
if student == "yes":
    discount = percent_of(subtotal, STUDENT_DISCOUNT_PERCENT)
else:
    discount = 0
net = subtotal - discount
# Simulation rules: tax AND tip use the discounted subtotal, not each other.
tax = percent_of(net, TAX_PERCENT)
tip = percent_of(net, tip_percent)
total = net + tax + tip

print("CAMPUS CAFE | INVOICE")
print(f"Customer: {customer}")
print(receipt_lines, end="")
print(f"Subtotal: {money(subtotal)}")
print(f"Discount: -{money(discount)}")
print(f"After discount: {money(net)}")
print(f"Tax: {money(tax)}")
print(f"Tip: {money(tip)}")
print(f"TOTAL: {money(total)}")

projects.title: Movie Ticket Kiosk
projects.description: Sell adult, child, and senior tickets. Apply matinee pricing and a fee for each ticket.
projects.focus: A fee per ticket is different from a fee per order.
rules: Adult tickets cost $12.00, child tickets $8.00, and senior tickets $9.00 before discounts.
A matinee receives 20% off ticket prices; an evening order receives no discount.
The 7% practice tax applies to discounted tickets. The $1.50 booking fee applies to every ticket and is untaxed in this simulation.
Zero tickets means zero ticket charges, tax, and fees. Round percentage amounts to the nearest cent, half up.
projects.formula: subtotal − discount + tax + ticket count × fee
projects.pseudocode:
READ customer
SET subtotal and ticket count to 0
REPEAT for each of 3 ticket categories
    READ quantity
    ADD line total and count tickets
READ matinee status
IF matinee, calculate discount
CALCULATE net, tax, and per-ticket fees
PRINT the invoice

walk.title: Model the transaction
walk.explanation: Identify two running totals: money spent and tickets sold. Both are needed because tax depends on price while the booking fee depends on quantity.

walk.title: Use expressions precisely
walk.explanation: BOOKING_FEE = 150 means $1.50 per ticket. A three-ticket order needs 150 × 3 = 450 cents in fees.

walk.title: Normalize customer answers
walk.explanation: strip() removes accidental spaces. lower() turns YES into yes. Strings also build the itemized receipt one line at a time.
walk.snippet:
matinee = input().strip().lower()
receipt_lines = receipt_lines + f"{name}: {quantity} x {money(price)} = {money(amount)}\n"

walk.title: Select a category and price
walk.explanation: if / elif / else chooses adult, child, or senior pricing. A separate if decides whether the whole order gets a matinee discount.

walk.title: Trace two accumulators
walk.explanation: On the default order, ticket_count becomes 2, then 3, then 3. subtotal becomes 2400, then 3200, then 3200 cents.
walk.snippet:
ticket_count = ticket_count + quantity
subtotal = subtotal + amount

walk.title: Call one function in two ways
walk.explanation: The same multiplication function calculates ticket lines and booking fees. Parameters describe roles; argument values can change between calls.
walk.snippet:
line_total(1200, 2)  # 2400 cents for adult tickets
line_total(150, 3)   # 450 cents for booking fees

# MOVIE TICKET KIOSK | Introduction to Python | Professor Porras
# Classroom simulation: prices are cents; rates are whole percentages.
# Input order: customer, adult qty, child qty, senior qty, matinee yes/no.
# Example input: Alex / 2 / 1 / 0 / yes (one value per line).

ADULT_PRICE = 1200
CHILD_PRICE = 800
SENIOR_PRICE = 900
TAX_PERCENT = 7
MATINEE_DISCOUNT_PERCENT = 20
BOOKING_FEE = 150

def money(cents):
    return f"${cents / 100:.2f}"

def percent_of(cents, percent):
    # Nearest cent, with half cents rounded up for nonnegative amounts.
    return (cents * percent + 50) // 100

def line_total(price, quantity):
    return price * quantity

def read_whole(label, minimum, maximum):
    while True:
        text = input().strip()
        if text.isascii() and text.isdigit():
            value = int(text)
            if minimum <= value <= maximum:
                return value
        print(f"Invalid {label}. Next input must be {minimum} to {maximum}.")

customer = input().strip()
if customer == "":
    customer = "Guest"
subtotal = 0
ticket_count = 0
receipt_lines = ""

# MODULE 5: count tickets and accumulate their prices across three categories.
for category in range(1, 4):
    if category == 1:
        name = "Adult"
        price = ADULT_PRICE
    elif category == 2:
        name = "Child"
        price = CHILD_PRICE
    else:
        name = "Senior"
        price = SENIOR_PRICE
    quantity = read_whole(name + " quantity", 0, 99)
    amount = line_total(price, quantity)
    ticket_count = ticket_count + quantity
    subtotal = subtotal + amount
    receipt_lines = receipt_lines + f"{name}: {quantity} x {money(price)} = {money(amount)}\n"

matinee = input().strip().lower()
while matinee != "yes" and matinee != "no":
    print("Matinee status: next input must be yes or no.")
    matinee = input().strip().lower()
if matinee == "yes":
    discount = percent_of(subtotal, MATINEE_DISCOUNT_PERCENT)
else:
    discount = 0
net = subtotal - discount
# Simulation rules: tax applies to discounted tickets. Booking fees are untaxed.
tax = percent_of(net, TAX_PERCENT)
fee = line_total(BOOKING_FEE, ticket_count)
total = net + tax + fee

print("CAMPUS CINEMA | INVOICE")
print(f"Customer: {customer}")
print(receipt_lines, end="")
print(f"Tickets: {ticket_count}")
print(f"Subtotal: {money(subtotal)}")
print(f"Discount: -{money(discount)}")
print(f"After discount: {money(net)}")
print(f"Tax: {money(tax)}")
print(f"Booking fee: {money(fee)}")
print(f"TOTAL: {money(total)}")

projects.title: Campus Bookstore Checkout
projects.description: Combine membership discounts, purchase thresholds, pickup, and shipping rules.
projects.focus: Test just below, exactly at, and above a threshold.
rules: Members receive 10% off only when the original subtotal is at least $50.00. Both conditions must be true.
The 7% practice tax applies to the discounted subtotal.
Pickup is free. Delivery is free at an after-discount subtotal of at least $75.00; otherwise shipping is $5.00. Shipping is untaxed in this simulation.
An order with zero items has no shipping charge. Round percentage amounts to the nearest cent, half up.
projects.pseudocode:
READ customer
REPEAT for 3 products: read quantity and add line totals
READ membership and pickup choices
IF member AND subtotal ≥ $50, apply discount
CALCULATE net and tax
IF empty order OR pickup OR net ≥ $75
    shipping = 0
ELSE shipping = $5
PRINT the invoice

walk.title: Write the rules first
walk.explanation: The discount threshold uses the original subtotal; the free-shipping threshold uses the after-discount subtotal. Name those two values to avoid mixing them up.

walk.title: Represent thresholds as numbers
walk.explanation: 5000 cents means $50.00. >= includes the boundary itself. Changing DISCOUNT_MINIMUM changes when membership saves money.

walk.title: Reuse string cleanup
walk.explanation: read_yes_no converts both answers to clean, lowercase text and repeats invalid values. Customer names keep their original capitalization.

walk.title: Combine Boolean conditions
walk.explanation: and requires both membership and enough spending. or makes shipping free when any listed condition is true. Parenthesize conditions when it helps you read the rule.

walk.title: Repeat and count accurately
walk.explanation: The for loop processes each product once. item_count identifies a truly empty cart, even if an item price is changed to zero.
walk.snippet:
item_count = item_count + quantity
subtotal = subtotal + amount

walk.title: Separate input from calculation
walk.explanation: read_yes_no validates text; percent_of performs arithmetic; money formats output. Small functions have one clear job and can be reused.
walk.snippet:
member = read_yes_no("Membership")
pickup = read_yes_no("Pickup")
tax = percent_of(net, TAX_PERCENT)

projects.code:
# CAMPUS BOOKSTORE CHECKOUT | Introduction to Python | Professor Porras
# Classroom simulation: prices and thresholds are cents; rates are percentages.
# Input order: customer, notebook qty, pen qty, textbook qty, member yes/no, pickup yes/no.
# Example input: Alex / 2 / 3 / 1 / yes / no (one value per line).

NOTEBOOK_PRICE = 600
PEN_PRICE = 200
TEXTBOOK_PRICE = 4000
TAX_PERCENT = 7
MEMBER_DISCOUNT_PERCENT = 10
DISCOUNT_MINIMUM = 5000
SHIPPING_FEE = 500
FREE_SHIPPING_MINIMUM = 7500

def money(cents):
    return f"${cents / 100:.2f}"

def percent_of(cents, percent):
    # Nearest cent, with half cents rounded up for nonnegative amounts.
    return (cents * percent + 50) // 100

def line_total(price, quantity):
    return price * quantity

def read_whole(label, minimum, maximum):
    while True:
        text = input().strip()
        if text.isascii() and text.isdigit():
            value = int(text)
            if minimum <= value <= maximum:
                return value
        print(f"Invalid {label}. Next input must be {minimum} to {maximum}.")

def read_yes_no(label):
    answer = input().strip().lower()
    while answer != "yes" and answer != "no":
        print(f"{label}: next input must be yes or no.")
        answer = input().strip().lower()
    return answer

customer = input().strip()
if customer == "":
    customer = "Guest"
subtotal = 0
item_count = 0
receipt_lines = ""
for item in range(1, 4):
    if item == 1:
        name = "Notebook"
        price = NOTEBOOK_PRICE
    elif item == 2:
        name = "Pen"
        price = PEN_PRICE
    else:
        name = "Textbook"
        price = TEXTBOOK_PRICE
    quantity = read_whole(name + " quantity", 0, 99)
    amount = line_total(price, quantity)
    item_count = item_count + quantity
    subtotal = subtotal + amount
    receipt_lines = receipt_lines + f"{name}: {quantity} x {money(price)} = {money(amount)}\n"

member = read_yes_no("Membership")
pickup = read_yes_no("Pickup")
# Both conditions must be true. Test exactly at DISCOUNT_MINIMUM, too.
if member == "yes" and subtotal >= DISCOUNT_MINIMUM:
    discount = percent_of(subtotal, MEMBER_DISCOUNT_PERCENT)
else:
    discount = 0
net = subtotal - discount
tax = percent_of(net, TAX_PERCENT)
# Simulation rules: shipping is untaxed; empty orders have no shipping charge.
if item_count == 0 or pickup == "yes" or net >= FREE_SHIPPING_MINIMUM:
    shipping = 0
else:
    shipping = SHIPPING_FEE
total = net + tax + shipping

print("CAMPUS BOOKSTORE | INVOICE")
print(f"Customer: {customer}")
print(receipt_lines, end="")
print(f"Subtotal: {money(subtotal)}")
print(f"Discount: -{money(discount)}")
print(f"After discount: {money(net)}")
print(f"Tax: {money(tax)}")
print(f"Shipping: {money(shipping)}")
print(f"TOTAL: {money(total)}")
